en: to be realized; to be materialized

examples.en: My childhood dream finally came true.
This plan will be realized next year.

examples.ko: 네가 말한 모든 소원이 실현되면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope every wish you mentioned comes true.
Goals aren't realized by talking alone.
I cried to see the dream that had come true.

examples.ko: 그 약속은 생각보다 빨리 실현돼서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: That promise was fulfilled sooner than I thought, which surprised me.

explain: '이루어지다'가 일상 말이고, '실현되다'는 꿈, 계획, 목표가 현실이 될 때 조금 격식 있게 써요. 앞에는 '꿈이', '계획이'처럼 '이/가'가 와요. 스스로 이루려는 쪽은 '실현하다'예요.

phrases.example: 열심히 하면 목표가 실현될 수 있어요.
phrases.en: If you work hard, your goal can be realized.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가능성을 말할 때 '-ㄹ 수 있다'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-ㄹ 수 있다' to talk about possibility.

phrases.en: That promise has not been realized yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계획이나 약속이 아직 현실이 되지 못했을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a plan or promise has not yet become real.

phrases.en: I hope everyone's wishes come true.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바람이나 소원을 말할 때 '-기를 바라다'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with '-기를 바라다' to express a wish or hope.

explain_en: Something comes true by itself — dreams, plans (꿈이 실현되다) 이루어지다 is the everyday word; 실현되다 is a bit more formal for dreams, plans, and goals becoming real. The subject takes 이/가, as in '꿈이 실현되다'. The active form, making it happen yourself, is 실현하다.

en: to fret; to be fussy; to be impatient

examples.ko: 시험 결과가 궁금해서 안달해 봤자 소용없어요.
examples.en: There is no use fretting just because you are curious about the exam result.

examples.ko: 그렇게 안달하지 말고 조금만 기다려 보세요.
examples.en: Don't fret so much, just wait a little.

examples.ko: 동생은 새 게임이 나오기만 기다리며 안달해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is fretting, just waiting for the new game to come out.

examples.ko: 아이가 장난감을 사 달라고 안달하는 모습이 귀여웠어요.
examples.en: It was cute to see the child fussing for me to buy a toy.
Fretting will not make the work finish faster.

examples.ko: 그는 승진하려고 안달하다가 오히려 실수를 했어요.
examples.en: He was so anxious to get promoted that he actually made a mistake.

explain: 단순히 '기다리다'가 아니라 마음이 급해서 가만히 있지 못하는 느낌이에요. '안달이 나다', '안달을 하다'처럼도 말하고, 보통 '-고 싶어서', '-아 달라고' 같은 이유와 함께 써요.

phrases.en: I was so curious about the gift that I couldn't sit still.
phrases.nuance_ko: '안달하다'보다 마음이 급해진 상태를 하나의 표현으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses the state of becoming impatient as a set phrase.

phrases.example: 너무 안달하지 마세요, 곧 좋은 소식이 올 거예요.
phrases.en: Don't be so anxious; good news will come soon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조급해하는 사람에게 부드럽게 말릴 때 쓰는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form for gently telling someone not to be so impatient.

phrases.example: 아이가 장난감을 사 달라고 안달을 해요.
phrases.en: The child is fussing for me to buy a toy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원하는 것을 얻으려고 보채는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone fussing to get what they want.

explain_en: Restless fretting over something wanted or awaited (저는 시험 결과가 나올 때까지 안달하며 기다렸어요.) 안달하다 means being so impatient that you can't stay still. You can also say '안달이 나다' or '안달을 하다'. It usually comes with a reason, such as wanting something or asking for it.

t90.ax: Don't fret so much, just wait a little.

examples.en: Watching the World Cup, patriotism arises on its own.
He is a person with strong patriotism.

examples.ko: 애국심은 말보다 행동으로 보여 주는 거예요.
examples.en: Patriotism is shown through actions rather than words.

examples.ko: 외국에 살면 오히려 애국심이 더 커져요.
examples.en: Living abroad makes your patriotism grow even more.
Advertisements often use patriotism.
The harder the times, the more people's patriotism comes together.

explain: 나라를 사랑하는 마음이에요. '애국'이 행동이나 태도라면 '애국심'은 마음 쪽에 더 가까워요. '애국심이 강하다/크다', '애국심을 키우다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: My grandfather is very patriotic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 성격이나 마음을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a person's character or feelings.

phrases.en: Schools try to nurture patriotism in children.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음을 일부러 길러 줄 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when deliberately nurturing the feeling.

phrases.example: 그 말은 애국심이 없다는 뜻이 아니에요.
phrases.en: That doesn't mean he has no patriotism.
phrases.nuance_ko: 애국심이 없는 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone lacks patriotism.

explain_en: It is the feeling of love for one's country. 애국 leans toward action or attitude, while 애국심 is closer to the feeling. Typical phrases are 애국심이 강하다 and 애국심을 키우다.

en: not even daring to dream of it; being out of the question

examples.en: Buying an expensive car is out of the question for me.
With such a small salary, overseas travel was beyond my dreams.

examples.ko: 언감생심, 제가 어떻게 그런 자리를 바라겠어요.
examples.en: How could I even dare hope for such a position?

examples.ko: 집 한 채 갖는 건 언감생심 꿈도 못 꿔요.
examples.en: Owning a house is something I wouldn't even dare to dream of.
In this situation, studying abroad is out of the question.

examples.ko: 그 큰 상을 받으리라고는 언감생심 생각도 못 했어요.
examples.en: I wouldn't have dared even to imagine winning that big prize.

explain: 형편이나 처지 때문에 감히 바랄 수도 없는 일을 말할 때 써요. '…은 언감생심이다'로도 쓰고, 문장 앞에서 '언감생심 꿈도 못 꾸다'처럼 부사처럼도 써요. 조금 예스럽고 겸손하거나 자조하는 말투예요.

phrases.example: 집을 사는 건 언감생심 꿈도 못 꿔요.
phrases.en: Buying a house is something I wouldn't even dare to dream of.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문장 앞에서 부사처럼 써서 꿈도 꿀 수 없다는 뜻을 강하게 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used like an adverb at the start to strengthen 'can't even dream of it'.

phrases.en: Back then, going to college was unthinkable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지난 일을 말할 때 과거형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, for talking about something from before.

phrases.en: I thought studying abroad was out of my reach.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 감히 바랄 수 없다고 여겼다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you assumed you couldn't dare to hope for it.

explain_en: It is used for something you cannot even dare to hope for because of your circumstances. It works as '…은 언감생심이다', and also at the front of a sentence like an adverb, as in '언감생심 꿈도 못 꾸다'. It sounds a little old-fashioned, modest or self-deprecating.

en: to mistake; to misunderstand; to misidentify

examples.en: It was dark, so I mistook my friend for someone else.

examples.ko: 그 말을 칭찬으로 오인하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't mistake that remark for a compliment.

examples.ko: 직원이 저를 손님으로 오인해서 인사를 했어요.
examples.en: A staff member mistook me for a customer and greeted me.

examples.ko: 이 광고는 소비자가 상품 효과를 오인하게 만들어요.
examples.en: This ad makes consumers misjudge the product's effect.
Some people mistake kindness for romantic interest.
I hope you haven't misunderstood what I meant.

explain: '착각하다'와 비슷하지만 'A를 B로 오인하다'처럼 어떤 것을 다른 것으로 잘못 보거나 잘못 알 때 써요. 조금 딱딱해서 뉴스나 글에 많고, 일상 대화에서는 '착각하다', '잘못 알다'를 더 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: I mistook sugar for salt and ruined the dish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 'A를 B로 오인하다'의 모양을 보여 주는 쓰임으로, 어떤 것을 다른 것으로 잘못 알 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This shows the pattern 'A를 B로 오인하다,' used when you wrongly take one thing for another.

phrases.en: The two words are similar, so they are easy to mix up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷해서 잘못 알기 쉬운 것을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain things that look alike and are easy to get wrong.

phrases.en: I mistook my bag for my friend's bag.
phrases.nuance_ko: '오인하다'보다 일상적이라서 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is more everyday than 오인하다 and used more often in conversation.

explain_en: Formal — wrongly take X for Y, by sight (친구로 오인하다) Similar to '착각하다', but it is used in the pattern 'A를 B로 오인하다', meaning to wrongly take one thing for another. It sounds a bit formal, so it is common in news and writing, while in conversation people more often say '착각하다' or '잘못 알다'.

en: to bear a grudge against; to feel resentment at; to resent

examples.en: My friend broke a promise, so I resented him.
Please don't resent me.
The child went into the room resenting the parents.

examples.ko: 시험에 떨어지고 제 자신을 원망하게 됐어요.
examples.en: After failing the exam, I ended up blaming myself.
Make your next plan instead of wasting time resenting.

examples.ko: 오래전에 헤어진 사람을 원망한 적은 없어요.
examples.en: I have never held a grudge against the person I parted from long ago.

explain: '원망하다'는 상대에게 섭섭하고 화난 마음을 오래 품는 거예요. '미워하다'는 싫은 감정 자체이고, '탓하다'는 잘못을 그 사람에게 돌리는 행동이에요. 보통 '누구를 원망하다'로 써요.

phrases.en: I resent the friend who didn't help me then.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원망하는 마음이 드는 상태를 말해요. 원망하는 대상 뒤에 '이/가'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the state of feeling resentment, with the target marked by '이/가'.

phrases.en: Don't blame other people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감정보다 잘못을 남에게 돌리는 행동에 가까워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Closer to the act of blaming someone than to the feeling.

phrases.example: 그는 원망 섞인 눈으로 저를 봤어요.
phrases.en: He looked at me with resentful eyes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표정, 목소리, 눈빛에 원망이 느껴질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when resentment can be felt in the look, voice, or tone.

explain_en: '원망하다' is to carry hurt, angry feelings toward someone for a long time. '미워하다' is just the feeling of hating, and '탓하다' is the act of putting the blame on someone. It is used as '누구를 원망하다'.

examples.en: I swear I'll pass this exam.
Nobody can guarantee the result.
He said so with full confidence.

examples.ko: 내일 비가 안 올 거라고 장담하기 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard to be sure it won't rain tomorrow.
My friend vouched that it was delicious and took me to the restaurant.
Don't be so quick to say you're sure.

explain: '약속하다'는 앞으로 하겠다고 정하는 것이고, '장담하다'는 틀림없다고 자신 있게 말하는 거예요. 그래서 '장담할 수 없다', '장담하기 어렵다'처럼 부정형으로 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 내일 비가 올지는 장담할 수 없어요.
phrases.en: I can't guarantee whether it will rain tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 확실하지 않을 때 가장 자주 쓰는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common negative form when something is uncertain.

phrases.en: This restaurant is good, I guarantee it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 틀림없다고 자신 있게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say with confidence that something is certain.

phrases.example: 그는 꼭 이길 수 있다고 자신 있게 말했어요.
phrases.en: He said confidently that he could surely win.
phrases.nuance_ko: '장담하다'를 쉬운 말로 풀어 쓴 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plain-language way to express 장담하다.

explain_en: Spoken: confidently assert an outcome, a personal bold promise. 약속하다 commits you to doing something; 장담하다 is saying with confidence that something is certain. That's why it often appears in negative forms like '장담할 수 없다' and '장담하기 어렵다'.

t90.ax: I swear I'll pass this exam.

en: to hate; to loathe; to detest

examples.en: He hates the person who deceived him.
War makes people hate each other.
The hatred I held for so long slowly melted away.
I want to live without hating anyone.

examples.ko: 아이는 자기를 괴롭힌 친구를 증오할 정도로 힘들어했어요.
examples.en: The child was so hurt that he came to hate the friend who bullied him.

examples.ko: 사람을 증오하면 내 마음이 먼저 힘들어져요.
examples.en: If you hate someone, your own heart suffers first.

explain: '싫어하다 < 미워하다 < 증오하다' 순서로 점점 강해져요. 증오하다는 아주 깊고 오래가는 미움이라서 말할 때는 거의 안 쓰고 글·뉴스·영화 대사에 나와요. 일상에서는 '너무 싫어요', '정말 미워요'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Please don't hate that person too much.
phrases.nuance_ko: 증오하다보다 약하고 일상에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Weaker than 증오하다 and used in daily speech.

phrases.en: I don't hate anyone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깊은 미움이 없다는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form: no deep hatred.

phrases.en: Hatred rose up in my heart.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미워하는 마음 자체를 말하는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for the feeling of hatred itself.

explain_en: Strong, deep hatred; more formal, also toward acts or evil. The strength goes 싫어하다 < 미워하다 < 증오하다. 증오하다 is deep, lasting hatred, so it is rare in everyday speech and mostly appears in writing, news and movie lines; in conversation people say '너무 싫어요' or '정말 미워요'.

t90.ax: War makes people hate each other.

en: to infer; to reason; to figure out

examples.en: Look at the clues and try to deduce the culprit.
The detective stayed up all night reasoning out the case.
I worked out the story just from the picture.

examples.ko: 추리할 수 있는 단서가 하나도 없어요.
examples.en: There is not a single clue to reason from.
If you reason through the situation, the answer will appear.

examples.ko: 말투를 보고 기분을 추리하는 건 어려워요.
examples.en: It is hard to figure out someone's mood from their tone.

explain: 단서를 모아 결론을 이끌어 낼 때 써요. 그냥 '맞혀 보다'와 달리 근거를 따져 본다는 느낌이에요. '~을/를 추리하다'로 쓰고, 명사 '추리'는 '추리 소설'에서 자주 만나요.

phrases.example: 이 사건의 범인이 누구인지 추리해 봅시다.
phrases.en: Let's try to deduce who the culprit in this case is.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 보다'로 한번 시도해 본다는 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-아/어 보다' adds the feel of giving it a try.

phrases.example: 이 단서로 범인을 추리할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can deduce the culprit from this clue.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄹ 수 있다'로 가능함을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-ㄹ 수 있다' expresses possibility.

phrases.en: Just as I deduced, he was the culprit.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ 대로'로 추리한 결과와 같다는 뜻을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-ㄴ 대로' says the result matched what was deduced.

explain_en: Work out an answer from clues, like solving a mystery (범인을 추리하다) Used when you gather clues and draw a conclusion. Unlike simply guessing ('맞혀 보다'), it feels like weighing evidence. It takes an object ('~을/를 추리하다'), and the noun 추리 is often met in '추리 소설'.

t90.ax: There is not a single clue to reason from.

examples.ko: 괜히 평지풍파를 일으키지 말고 조용히 넘어가요.
examples.en: Let's not stir up trouble for nothing and just let it pass quietly.

examples.ko: 평지풍파가 일어날까 봐 아무도 말을 못 했어요.
examples.en: Fearing it would stir up trouble, nobody could say anything.
That one remark was the start of all the trouble.

examples.ko: 잘 지내는 가족에게 평지풍파를 만들고 싶지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't want to cause trouble for a family that's getting along well.
I'm glad the matter ended without any fuss.
A small mistake grew into a big commotion.

explain: 평화로웠던 곳에 갑자기 생긴 소란이나 분쟁을 가리키는 한자성어예요. 주로 '평지풍파를 일으키다/일으키지 마'처럼 쓰고, 괜한 문제를 만든다는 비판의 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 회의에서 괜히 평지풍파를 일으켰어요.
phrases.en: He stirred up needless trouble at the meeting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 기본적인 짝말로, 조용하던 곳에 쓸데없는 소란을 만든다는 비판의 뜻이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pairing, with a critical sense of creating needless trouble where things were calm.

phrases.example: 작은 말다툼 때문에 집안에 평지풍파가 일어났어요.
phrases.en: A small quarrel caused a storm of trouble in the family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조용하던 곳에 갑자기 소란이 생겼다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an uproar suddenly breaks out where things were calm.

phrases.en: The meeting dragged on because of needless trouble.
phrases.nuance_ko: '괜한'을 앞에 붙이면 쓸데없다는 비판이 더 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '괜한' makes the criticism of its pointlessness clearer.

explain_en: This four-character idiom refers to a sudden disturbance or dispute in a place that was peaceful. It is mostly used as '평지풍파를 일으키다' or '평지풍파를 일으키지 마', with a critical tone about causing needless trouble.

en: to be deluded; to be deceived; to be misled

examples.ko: 광고에 현혹돼서 필요 없는 물건을 샀어요.
examples.en: I was taken in by an ad and bought something I didn't need.
Be careful not to be misled by fancy words.

examples.ko: 많은 사람이 가짜 뉴스에 쉽게 현혹돼요.
examples.en: Many people are easily deceived by fake news.

examples.ko: 겉모습에 현혹되면 진짜 좋은 것을 놓칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you're misled by appearances, you may miss the truly good thing.

examples.ko: 그는 달콤한 약속에 현혹되어 큰돈을 잃었어요.
examples.en: He was lured by sweet promises and lost a lot of money.

examples.ko: 동생은 친구의 말에 현혹돼서 계획을 바꿨어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling was swayed by a friend's words and changed the plan.

explain: 보통 '~에 현혹되다'처럼 조사 '에'와 함께 쓰고, 광고, 말, 겉모습처럼 마음을 흔드는 것 때문에 판단이 흐려진다는 나쁜 뜻이에요. '속다'보다 마음이 홀린 느낌이 강해요. 시험이나 글에서 '현혹되지 마라'라는 말로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: You must not be misled by sweet words.
phrases.nuance_ko: 듣기 좋은 말에 마음이 흔들려 판단을 잘못한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means your judgment gets clouded by pleasant-sounding words.

phrases.en: Children are easily misled by ads.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그런 일이 자주 생길 수 있다고 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that this kind of thing happens easily.

phrases.en: I was fooled by an ad and bought an expensive item.
phrases.nuance_ko: 더 쉬운 말이에요. '현혹되다'처럼 마음이 홀린 느낌은 약하고 그냥 속았다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler word; it just means being tricked, without the sense of being enchanted.

explain_en: Formal — passive, charmed or fooled by ads or tricks. It is usually used with the particle '에' as in '~에 현혹되다', and has a negative sense of judgment being clouded by things like ads, words or appearances. It feels more like being enchanted than simply '속다' (to be tricked). It often appears in writing and exams as '현혹되지 마라'.

examples.en: We installed a smoke detector at our house.
The detector went off, so everyone went outside.

examples.ko: 이 감지기는 움직임이 있으면 불이 켜져요.
examples.en: This sensor turns on the light when there is movement.

examples.ko: 문 앞 감지기에 손을 대면 문이 열려요.
examples.en: If you put your hand on the sensor by the door, it opens.
I check whether the gas detector is on.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 감지기로 사람이 있는지 확인해요.
examples.en: This building uses sensors to check whether anyone is there.

explain: '센서'와 거의 같은 말이에요. 일상에서는 '센서'를 더 흔하게 쓰고, '감지기'는 '화재 감지기', '연기 감지기', '움직임 감지기'처럼 안전 장치 이름에 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: A fire detector is attached to the ceiling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불이 난 것을 알려 주는 안전 장치를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A safety device that detects fire.

phrases.example: 현관에 움직임 감지기가 있어서 불이 켜져요.
phrases.en: There is a motion sensor at the entrance, so the light turns on.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 물건이 움직이는 것을 알아채는 장치예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A device that notices when someone or something moves.

phrases.en: When smoke appeared, the detector went off.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장치가 일하기 시작할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the device starts working.

explain_en: It is nearly the same as 센서. In daily life 센서 is more common, while 감지기 appears often in safety device names such as 화재 감지기 and 연기 감지기.

examples.ko: 아버지가 곡괭이로 땅을 파서 나무를 심으셨어요.
examples.en: My father dug the ground with a pickax and planted a tree.
The miners went into the tunnel carrying pickaxes.
Where did you put the pickax?

examples.ko: 단단한 땅은 삽보다 곡괭이가 더 편해요.
examples.en: For hard ground, a pickax is easier than a shovel.
I swung the pickax for a long time, so my arms hurt.
I borrowed a pickax and a shovel and made a small vegetable garden.

explain: 삽은 흙을 퍼서 옮길 때 쓰고, 곡괭이는 끝이 뾰족해서 단단한 땅이나 돌을 찍어 팔 때 써요. 땅을 파는 일을 '곡괭이질'이라고도 해요. 발음은 [곡꽹이]로 'ㄲ' 소리가 나요.

phrases.example: 하루 종일 곡괭이질을 했더니 팔이 아파요.
phrases.en: I swung the pickax all day and my arms hurt.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곡괭이로 땅을 파는 일 자체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the act of digging with a pickax.

phrases.en: You have to dig hard ground with a pickax.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단단한 땅이나 돌을 팔 때 쓰는 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural pairing for digging hard ground or rock.

phrases.en: There is a pickax and a shovel in the storage shed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅 파는 도구로 같이 말하는 경우가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The two are often mentioned together as digging tools.

explain_en: A shovel scoops and moves soil, while a pickax has a pointed end for breaking into hard ground or stone. The act of digging with it is called '곡괭이질'. It is pronounced [곡꽹이], with a tense 'ㄲ' sound.

examples.en: They printed the name on the invitation in gold leaf.

examples.ko: 이 책은 표지에 금박이 입혀져 있어요.
examples.en: This book has gold leaf on the cover.

examples.ko: 금박 글씨가 반짝반짝 빛나서 눈에 띄어요.
examples.en: The gold-leaf letters sparkle and stand out.

examples.ko: 한복 치마에 금박 무늬가 들어가 있어요.
examples.en: The hanbok skirt has a gold-leaf pattern on it.
It is old, so the gold leaf has peeled off in places.

examples.ko: 선물 상자에 금박 리본을 달아서 예뻐 보여요.
examples.en: The gift box looks pretty with the gold-foil ribbon on it.

explain: 금을 아주 얇게 편 것, 또는 그런 금색 장식을 붙이거나 찍은 것을 말해요. 그냥 '금색'과 달리 책 표지, 한복, 초대장 같은 곳에 반짝이게 입힌 장식에 써요.

phrases.en: The craftsman applied gold leaf to the book cover.
phrases.nuance_ko: 금박 장식을 붙이는 일을 말할 때 가장 자연스러운 동사 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural verb pairing for applying gold leaf decoration.

phrases.example: 초대장에 금박 글씨로 이름이 쓰여 있어요.
phrases.en: My name is written on the invitation in gold lettering.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반짝이는 금색으로 찍거나 쓴 글씨를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to letters stamped or written in shiny gold.

phrases.example: 이 한복에는 금박 장식이 있어서 화려해요.
phrases.en: This hanbok has gold-leaf decoration, so it looks splendid.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옷이나 물건에 붙인 금색 무늬를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for gold patterns attached to clothes or objects.

explain_en: It refers to gold beaten very thin, or gold-colored decoration applied or stamped on something. Unlike plain '금색' (gold color), it is used for shiny decoration on things like book covers, hanbok and invitations.
